wording: **Every business (Unternehmer) taxed in Germany files an annual VAT return** for the calendar year, electronically, in which it computes the tax or the surplus itself (§ 18(3) UStG). The tax period is the calendar year (§ 16(1) UStG), or the part of it in which the business traded (§ 16(3)). The return counts as a tax assessment subject to review (§ 168 AO), so no notice follows unless the tax office departs from it. If the return lowers the tax below the prepayments or shows a refund, that effect starts only when the tax office agrees, which needs no form; the refund is then paid without a separate claim (§ 168 sentences 2 and 3 AO; USt 2 E 2026, lines 124 to 126).

wording: - **A small business using § 19 UStG.** § 19(1) sentence 2 switches off the filing duties of § 18(1) to (4) UStG, which includes the annual return. This applies from tax year 2024 (§ 27(39) UStG). Two exceptions keep a return due: the tax office asks for one (§ 149(1) sentence 2 AO), or the business owes tax as a buyer, for example under reverse charge or on an intra-Community acquisition (§ 18(4a) UStG). The 2026 form instructions say the same.

wording: - **A foreign business whose only German supplies go through the one-stop shop.** For those supplies § 18(1) to (4) does not apply (§ 18j(4) sentence 4 UStG).

wording: **The small business scheme (§ 19 UStG, rules in force since 1 January 2025).** A business based in Germany makes tax-free supplies if its total turnover was not above EUR 25,000 in the previous calendar year and is not above EUR 100,000 in the current year. Tax-free means no VAT on invoices and no input tax deduction. Total turnover (Gesamtumsatz, § 19(2)) is counted on receipts and leaves out sales of fixed assets and some exempt supplies. Three rules decide most cases (UStAE 19.1):
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - Previous year above EUR 25,000: standard taxation from 1 January of the current year, even if the current year stays low.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - Previous year within EUR 25,000: the scheme runs until current-year turnover passes EUR 100,000. The supply that crosses the line is already taxed in full, and from then on normal invoicing, input tax and advance returns apply.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - First year of business: the limit is EUR 25,000 in the current year, not EUR 100,000. The supply that crosses EUR 25,000 is already taxed.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: A small business can give up the scheme by a statement to the tax office up to the last day of February of the second year after the year concerned. The waiver binds for at least five calendar years and can then be revoked from the start of a later calendar year (§ 19(3)).

wording: **The EU small business scheme.** A German business seeking the small business exemption in another member state must apply electronically for the special reporting procedure at the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (BZSt), which issues a small-business identification number (§ 19a(1) UStG). Its EU-wide annual turnover must not exceed EUR 100,000 in either the previous or current year; it must also meet the actual exemption conditions of each host state and the no-duplicate-procedure-registration condition in § 19a(1) no. 4. A BZSt number and the EU turnover test alone do not establish host-state exemption. It files a quarterly turnover report with the BZSt within one month after each quarter (§ 19a(3)). It must tell the BZSt within 15 working days if EU turnover passes EUR 100,000; participation ends at that point (§ 19a(4)). A business based elsewhere in the EU can use Germany's exemption only if the incorporated German § 19(1) limits also hold: German total turnover under § 19(2) at most EUR 25,000 in the preceding year and at most EUR 100,000 in the current year. It additionally needs EU-wide annual turnover at most EUR 100,000 in both years and the home-state small-business number valid for that German exemption (§ 19(4)).
disposition: R23–25 bounded source-backed condition successor

wording: **Cash accounting (Istversteuerung, § 20 UStG).** The normal rule taxes supplies when they are made (Sollversteuerung, § 16(1)). On application the tax office can let a business tax receipts instead if any one of these holds: total turnover of the previous year was not more than EUR 800,000; the business is released from bookkeeping under § 148 AO; or, for those supplies only, it practises a liberal profession under § 18(1) no. 1 EStG. Input tax is not affected: it is deductible once the supply is made and the invoice is held, not when it is paid (§ 15(1) no. 1 UStG). Only VAT on a payment made before the supply waits for both the invoice and the payment.

wording: **The annual return is a full recomputation, not a sum of the quarters.** Under § 18(3) UStG the business recomputes the year's tax from § 16(1) to (4) and § 17 UStG: output tax on the year's supplies, plus tax owed as a buyer, minus deductible input tax, plus or minus input tax corrections. The advance returns are only prepayments on it. So the annual return is where errors in the advance returns are put right, where § 15a corrections of up to EUR 6,000 are normally made (§ 44(3) UStDV; its sentence 2 requires sale/§ 3(1b) disposal corrections in the advance return for the period of disposal), and where a partial-exemption key estimated during the year is replaced with the final one.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: **How the 2026 form (USt 2 A) ends.** Section K collects the totals. Line 124 (Kz 816) is the remaining tax or surplus for the year. Line 125 is the prepayment total for 2026, the "Vorauszahlungssoll", including any special prepayment. Line 126 (Kz 820) is the balance: line 124 minus line 125. A positive balance is the closing payment (Abschlusszahlung); a negative one is a refund. Line 125 is what was declared or assessed for the advance returns, not what was actually paid; late or missing payments are chased separately.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: **The special prepayment in the annual figures.** A monthly filer with the one-month extension pays 1/11 of the previous year's advance payments by 10 February (§§ 47, 48(2) UStDV). It is credited in the last advance return of the year (§ 48(4) UStDV) and so it sits inside the line 125 total. A quarterly filer pays none.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: **Small business: what counts.** Total turnover is the sum of taxable supplies counted on receipts, less the two distinct exempt-supply categories in § 19(2): no. 1 subtracts supplies exempt under § 4 no. 8(i), no. 9(b) and nos. 11–29; no. 2 subtracts supplies exempt under § 4 no. 8(a)–(h), no. 9(a) and no. 10 only if they are ancillary supplies (Hilfsumsätze). Main financial or insurance activity in that second category is not automatically subtracted; establish ancillary status from the actual activity, without an invented numerical test. Sales of fixed assets are excluded separately. Supplies on which the customer owes the tax under § 13b count in; services the small business buys under § 13b do not (UStAE 19.2(2)). A small business still owes VAT on imports, intra-Community acquisitions and reverse-charge purchases (UStAE 19.1(1)).
disposition: R23–25 bounded source-backed condition successor

wording: **Moving into standard taxation.** When a small business moves into standard taxation, a supply made in the new year is taxed in full even if the customer paid in advance in the old year. That after-tax goes in line 39 (Kz 317) of the annual return and in line 46 (Kz 65) of the advance return for the period of the supply (USt 1 E 2026, line 46). A supply made in the small-business year stays tax-free even when it is paid later. Input tax on assets bought while exempt can come back over the § 15a period: the 2026 form lists a change of scheme under the small business rules as a change in circumstances for § 15a (USt 2 A, line 100).
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: **Cash accounting.** The tax arises when the fee is received. When the method changes, no supply may be taxed twice or escape tax (§ 20 sentence 3). A supply made in a cash-accounting year stays on cash accounting if it is paid after a later switch to accruals (USt 2 A 2026 instructions, line 21).
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: **Partial exemption (§ 15(4) UStG).** When a purchase is used for both taxable supplies and exempt supplies that bar deduction, the share linked to the exempt supplies is not deductible. Allocate directly where you can. Use a reasonable estimate otherwise. Split by turnover only if no more precise economic allocation is possible. For buildings, split by floor area unless another method is more precise. The share is fixed for the year in the annual return.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: **Input tax correction (§ 15a UStG).** If the use of an asset changes within five years of first use (ten years for land and buildings), the input tax deducted on it is corrected by one fifth (or one tenth) a year for each year of change (§ 15a(1) and (5)). For a still usable asset used more than once, a sale or deemed supply under § 3(1b) before the correction period ends is also a change if its VAT treatment differs from the use governing the original input-tax deduction (§ 15a(8)). A sale taxed on the same basis as the original fully taxable use does not trigger that disposal adjustment merely because the asset is sold. Under § 15a(9), a qualifying disposal is treated as continued business use on the corresponding changed basis for the remaining correction period. The UStDV simplifications are in the table: nothing where input tax on the acquisition or production cost is not more than EUR 1,000, nothing for a change under 10 points unless above EUR 1,000, and generally only in the annual return up to EUR 6,000. If the asset is sold or supplied under § 3(1b) during the correction period, § 44(3) sentence 2 instead requires the corrections for the disposal year and the remaining years in the advance return for the period of disposal, even when the amount is no more than EUR 6,000.
disposition: R23–25 bounded source-backed condition successor

wording: **Domestic reverse charge (§ 13b UStG).** The customer owes the tax for, among others, services from EU suppliers under § 3a(2), works and services from foreign suppliers, construction services to a business that itself provides construction services, building cleaning on the same basis, and mobile phones, tablets and chips from EUR 5,000. The customer declares output tax and, if entitled, deducts the same amount as input tax. A small business that receives such services owes the tax and cannot deduct it. The boxes and the supplier patterns are in [germany-vat-return](germany-vat-return.md).

wording: **How to file.** The annual return goes to the local tax office electronically, authenticated, through ELSTER (§ 18(3) UStG; § 87a(6) AO). Paper only with permission, to avoid hardship. Foreign businesses add Anlage UN. The one-stop shop return goes to the BZSt through the BZSt online portal.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: **One-stop shop (§ 18j UStG).** A business established only in Germany that sells goods at a distance or supplies telecom, broadcasting or electronic services to consumers in other member states charges the customer's country's VAT once the EU-wide total passes EUR 10,000 (§ 3c(4)); the very sale that crosses it is the first one. Instead of registering in each country it can declare that VAT quarterly through the one-stop shop at the BZSt. The notice to take part must reach the BZSt before the quarter from which the scheme is used (§ 18j(1) sentence 3), so registration normally starts on the first day of the quarter after the application. Taking part covers all member states and all such supplies. Corrections to an OSS return within three years go in a later OSS return. Repeated late filing leads to exclusion (§ 18j(6)).
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - **Late annual return.** The tax office may set a late filing surcharge (§ 152(1) AO). It must set one if the return is not filed within 14 months after the year ends, for 2026 by 29 February 2028, unless the tax office extended the deadline or the tax is nil, negative or not above the prepayments (§ 152(2) no. 1 and (3)). The amount is 0.25% per started month of the tax less the prepayments, at least EUR 25 per started month, capped at EUR 25,000 (§ 152(5) sentence 2 and (10)). For the monthly or quarterly advance returns the amount is discretionary instead (§ 152(8)).
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - **Late payment.** 1% per started month on the overdue tax rounded down to a multiple of EUR 50 (§ 240(1) AO). This runs on a late closing payment and on late advance payments.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - **Interest.** Where an assessment differs from the prepayments, the difference carries 0.15% for each full month from 1 April 2028 for tax year 2026 (§ 233a(2) AO, 15 months after the year end; § 238(1a) AO).
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - **Fines.** Not paying an advance payment, a closing balance or an OSS payment in full and on time is an administrative offence with a fine up to EUR 30,000 (§ 26a(1) and (3) UStG). Deliberately or recklessly not issuing a required invoice, or not keeping invoices for eight years: up to EUR 5,000. Deliberately or recklessly not keeping, for two years, the invoices and payment records that § 14b(1) sentence 5 requires: up to EUR 1,000 (§ 26a(2) nos. 1 to 3 and (3)).
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - **Correcting an error.** An error in an advance return can be corrected in the annual return, as in Example 1. Deliberate under-declaration is tax evasion and outside this skill.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

wording: - **EU businesses using the German small business exemption** need the home-state small-business number valid for Germany, EU-wide annual turnover at most EUR 100,000 in both previous and current years, and the incorporated German § 19(1) total-turnover limits of EUR 25,000 in the preceding year and EUR 100,000 in the current year (§ 19(4)). For example, EU turnover of EUR 80,000 and German turnover of EUR 30,000 in 2025 fail the German prior-year limb for 2026 despite a valid number; German turnover of exactly EUR 25,000 passes that limb only, subject to all other conditions. They waive the German exemption through their home state, not in Germany (§ 19(5)).

section: Example 1: A GmbH's 2026 annual return with one correction
wording: Muster GmbH is a quarterly filer on accruals, with no extension. Its four 2026 advance returns declared output tax of EUR 38,000 and input tax of EUR 29,750, so prepayments of EUR 8,250 (Q1 2,550, Q2 1,900, Q3 2,200, Q4 1,600). Preparing the annual return, the accountant finds a December 2026 sale of EUR 10,000 net, invoiced but booked in January 2027. It belongs to 2026. Output tax for the year is 38,000 + 1,900 = EUR 39,900. Line 124 (Kz 816) is 39,900 - 29,750 = EUR 10,150. Line 125 is EUR 8,250. Line 126 (Kz 820) is a closing payment of EUR 1,900.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

section: Example 1: A GmbH's 2026 annual return with one correction
wording: The GmbH files itself on Friday 14 May 2027, so the balance is due one month later, Monday 14 June 2027. If it paid two months late, the late payment surcharge would be 1% x 1,900 x 2 = EUR 38. If it had instead filed on 15 October 2027, three months started after the 2 August deadline. Should the tax office set a surcharge, 0.25% of 1,900 is EUR 4.75 a month, below the EUR 25 minimum, so 3 x 25 = EUR 75.

section: Example 2: A translator leaves the small business scheme and uses cash accounting
wording: Lena is a self-employed translator, a liberal profession under § 18(1) no. 1 EStG. Her 2024 total turnover was within EUR 25,000, so in 2025 she used § 19. Her total turnover for 2025 was EUR 31,200, counted on receipts and including the advance below (UStAE 19.2(1)). That is above EUR 25,000 but below EUR 100,000, so 2025 stayed tax-free and she filed no VAT return for it. Because 2025 passed EUR 25,000, every supply she makes from 1 January 2026 is taxed at 19%. Her 2025 turnover is far below EUR 800,000, and she is a liberal professional, so the tax office can let her tax receipts (§ 20 nos. 1 and 3); she applies for it.
disposition: Exact prior current unit with rebound native coordinates

section: Example 2: A translator leaves the small business scheme and uses cash accounting
wording: Her 2025 tax was nil, so she files quarterly (§ 18(2)). In Q1 2026 she receives EUR 8,925 for 2026 work (EUR 7,500 net plus EUR 1,425 VAT) and EUR 1,800 for a December 2025 job. The December job was supplied while she was exempt, so it carries no VAT. A client paid her EUR 2,000 in November 2025 as an advance for a job she delivered in February 2026. The supply is in 2026, so the advance is taxed in the period of the supply (USt 1 E 2026, line 46; USt 2 E 2026, line 39): 2,000 x 19 / 119 = EUR 319.33, in Kz 65 of the advance return and line 39 (Kz 317) of the annual return. Her input tax on 2026 invoices for the quarter is EUR 380. Q1 payment: 1,425 + 319.33 - 380 = EUR 1,364.33, due Friday 10 April 2026. She must already be able to receive e-invoices. For 2026 supplies she may still send paper invoices, or PDF invoices with the client's consent, to German business clients until 31 December 2026 (§ 27(38) no. 1); for 2027 supplies the relief continues to 31 December 2027 as long as her 2026 total turnover stays within EUR 800,000 (no. 2).
